newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's wage settlement levels fall - report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's wage settlement levels fall - report.

text.p: South African wage settlements for the nine months to September were slightly lower at 9.9 percent compared to 10.4 percent in the first six months of the year, according to a wage settlement survey.
Industrial relations consultants Andrew Levy & Associates said on Thursday the year-end figure was expected to match the 10 percent level, which was also reached in 1993 and 1994.
The report said the slightly lower figure indicated that unions were "moderating their demands in the light of the current economic reality".

"Wage negotiations this year have been tough, but they have been conducted in a good spirit with a view to reaching settlement. However, where there has been action, it has been particularily difficult," it said.
Strike action triggered by wages decreased in the nine months ending September compared to the same period last year.
"The general comment regarding union demands is that they are becoming more realistic and are within the realms of settlement," the report said.
In line with the recommendations in the new Employment Standards Act for the phasing in of a 40-hour week, many companies were reducing their working hours.
It said the delay in the implementation of the new Labour Relations Act was expected to cause confusion as the labour movement was geared up to exercise its new found rights.

Average settlement levels reached included 9.2 percent for the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa, 11.2 percent for the Transport and General Workers Union and 9.1 percent for the South African Clothing and Textile Workers Union.
